tagline: Doha Bay, The Pearl, Lusail and Al Wakrah — a state building its future on the waterfront, on calm Gulf water made for foiling.
summary: Qatar is a Gulf peninsula state whose population and marquee developments cluster along a sheltered coast — central Doha and its Corniche, the man-made islands of The Pearl and Banana Island, the new city of Lusail to the north, and the historic port town of Al Wakrah to the south. Water transport today is nascent — water taxis and tourist dhows — while the road corridors congest. With calm, shallow Gulf water and state-backed waterfront ambition, Qatar is a clean fit for a foiling network linking its coastal nodes.
why_marine_mobility: Qatar's marquee destinations line one sheltered coast — Doha, The Pearl, Lusail, Banana Island, Al Wakrah — minutes apart by water but slow by congested road. Navier's Pioneer II flies the whole mesh, silent and zero-emission off existing marinas and the Corniche, while the Quanta-LR range opens longer Gulf line-haul toward Qatar's offshore developments and the wider GCC coast. Signature corridors are bound to sealed route_ids in ROUTES.json (rebound 2026-07-12).

demand_signals.note: Doha's Corniche, dhow harbour and major-event calendar draw heavy visitor flows already oriented to the Gulf.

use_cases.body: A clean foiling commuter spine linking Al Wakrah and Lusail to central Doha along the calm Gulf coast, bypassing the congested road corridors.
On-demand premium hops between The Pearl, Banana Island, Lusail Marina and the Corniche — Qatar's marquee waterfront nodes, minutes apart by water.
Event-and-leisure shuttles across Doha Bay during Qatar's major-event calendar, on silent zero-emission craft.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: The entire Qatar coastal mesh — Doha Corniche↔The Pearl (~4 nm), Doha↔Lusail Marina (~6.5 nm), Doha↔Banana Island (~4.5 nm), Doha↔Al Wakrah (~11 nm), Lusail↔Pearl (~3.5 nm), Al Wakrah↔Banana Island (~9.5 nm) — sits well inside the 70 nm all-electric range on calm, shallow, sheltered Gulf water.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: The coastal network is pure Pioneer II territory; Quanta-LR hybrid range opens longer Gulf line-haul toward offshore developments and down the Saudi/UAE coast without charging dependency, integrating Qatar into a wider GCC corridor.

signature_routes.label: Doha Corniche ↔ The Pearl (all-electric waterfront hop)
Old Doha Port ↔ Al Wakrah Marina (southern bay link)

transit_planning: For Mwani Qatar, Qatar Tourism or a master-developer such as Qatari Diar/UDC: a clean water tier linking the Corniche, The Pearl, Lusail and Al Wakrah, integrated with the waterfront-development and tourism-diversification agenda under Qatar National Vision 2030.
competitive_landscape: Urban water transport is nascent — limited Doha Bay water taxis and tourist dhows, with no fast, clean, on-demand network linking the coastal nodes. There is no incumbent fast-ferry service to displace; the opportunity is to activate a calm, build-ready coast as part of Qatar's waterfront push.
regulatory_note: Maritime activity falls under the Ministry of Transport and Mwani Qatar (ports authority), with strong state backing for tourism-and-waterfront diversification under Qatar National Vision 2030. The calm, regulated Gulf coast and government-led marina and corniche development provide a supportive permitting environment.
seasonality: A winter-weighted leisure market (November–April) when Gulf temperatures are comfortable, with peak summer heat (June–September) favouring air-conditioned, low-energy electric cabins for commuter use. The sheltered Gulf is calm and navigable year-round, with only occasional summer shamal winds.
